Question:
In the hypotenuse diagram, the large square has side length \(c\), and four right triangles with legs \(a\) and \(b\) enclose a small square. How can \(a^2+b^2=c^2\) be obtained? (Assume \(b>a\) and select the correct derivation.)

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_175_q1_question_en.svg)
Solution: The area of the large square equals the areas of the 4 triangles plus the area of the small square in the center (with side length \(b-a\)): \(c^2=2ab+b^2-2ab+a^2=a^2+b^2\).
